Question: What is the theoretical difference between international "free trade" and domestic "free trade"?

Is there any reason that one should not be "free" and the other should be -- other than scale?

One difference is that it is never completely "free". For instance: China completely controlling their currency when other countries have openly traded market currencies. Also, countries control their trade in various other ways to give themselves an advantage.

If it was completely free, then there isn't much difference I suppose. However, giving money to a neighbor for goods or services is more likely to benefit you directly through positive side effects than sending money to a "neighbor" across the world.

Meaning is a tricky subject. Purpose and intent are factors, but outcomes define identify as much as intent. And since existence will occur across the live-span of the subject, many outcomes will be produced, and meaning could be derived from any set of these outcomes. Perhaps we must first define what set of outcomes we want to use to derive meaning? If so, we must consider the set of all outcomes as a possible definition. This is tricky because the term "all outcomes" requires a finality of "no further outcomes" to be considered and there for an implicit exclusion of derivative outcomes. Defined within this constrain, the question should be worded "what did Voat mean?", and this line of inquiry would be premature. More narrowly defining the question as "What has Voat meant so far?" would give us a smaller set of outcomes to consider and therefore likely more weight would fall on the intent, however the question is still ambiguous enough to be very difficult to answer beyond obvious intent of "reddit without censorship" by which was the initial intent of the creator. However, as the creators quickly discovered, they could not operate reddit without censorship, which quickly flung Voat into an identity crisis as the outcomes of the site were unable to stay in sync with the creator's intent. This has caused the transformation into the current state of "reddit, but smaller, without Pao, and slightly less censorship". Which may suffice as a meaning for voat at this point in time, but, don't forget, that meaning will change as the set of data to consider grows over time.
